items.title: Carter Benny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I don’t know that they had any contract musicians other than Lee Young, the drummer-percussionist, that was under contract to Columbia Studios.

ctx.x: I’d like to just ask you something about, again, the problems of the racial barriers in the studios that you may have encountered. You were often credited as being the first black musician-composer to break these barriers. I think there were some other people that were involved, like around the time William Grant Still, I think, was in Hollywood somewhat before you were there. Any other black composers or arrangers that you ran into who had been here doing anything before you began?

Well, there was Phil Moore, who was very busy in the studios. I don’t know exactly what he did. Prior to him, I understand there was an arranger named Will Votary [phonetic] that, you know, that it was a little before my time here. Then I don’t know that

they had any contract musicians other than Lee Young, the drummer-percussionist, that was under contract to Columbia Studios. Now, I don’t know that any other musicians or composers were under contract. Of course, I was never under contract, as it were. But I can’t say that I have to be credited for anything, you know, other than I’m credited for keeping alive and keeping my rent paid, gas in the car.

items.title: 53279_Lee Young Oral History Interview
items.q: Lionel Newman was very fond of Benny Carter... Benny used to do a lot of work at 20th Century Fox

ctx.x: Well, it couldn't have been that you were doing a bad job, or your contract wouldn't have been renewed.

Right. But anyway, I'm just saying, ever since I can remember, the closest anyone came to being on the staff was Lionel Newman was very fond of Benny Carter, you know -- very fond of Benny Carter. And when Benny Carter had his big band down here -- you know, Benny used to do a lot of work at 20th Century Fox, and they wanted him to come off the road with the band and wanted to give him a job there as a composer and arranger.

items.title: 66095_Benny Carter oral history interview
items.q: I know of one having been under contract was Lee Young... But of course, they don't have contract orchestras any more, but they did then. But they didn't have any blacks that I knew of, other than Lee Young.

ctx.x: Right. You got in to the studio orchestras. Did you get work in the studios as a conductor and so on around that time?

Yes. No, not as a conductor -- but I did do a bit of work as, you know, the player. I did a number of things as a player, and also as a player in the orchestra, and a player on screen with, you know, my own groups at different times.

But there were no blacks in the staff orchestras that were under contract. That's what I was trying to get to. And the only instance -- I know of one having been under contract was Lee Young, who is a percussionist and was with Columbia for some years, under contract. But of course, they don't have contract orchestras any more, but they did then. But they didn't have any blacks that I knew of, other than Lee Young.
